**Failure mode**
Wrong decomposition. One Agent is doing two jobs on different time horizons: a real-time job (read claim, look up, draft, send) and a multi-day follow-up cycle (wait, remind at 3 days, escalate at 7 days, then book the credit). A single Run can't sit idle for days, so it hit the idle timeout during the wait.

**Where it went wrong**
At transcript turn [4], right after Step 5 (send) and at Step 6 of the AOP ("Wait for the supplier's reply"). The first half of the work finished: the claim was sent in turn [1]. The Agent then polled Gmail once, found nothing, and had no way to wait three days inside the Run. Steps 7–14 never ran. That includes the 3-day reminder and the 7-day escalation, so this claim currently has no follow-up scheduled.

**Evidence**
- AOP: "6. Wait for the supplier's reply." / "7. If no reply after 3 days, send a reminder."
- Transcript: "[4] Agent: No reply yet. I'll keep checking." → "[5] System: Run stopped after idle timeout."

**Fix**
Split the AOP at Step 6 into two Agents:
- **Agent A (Steps 1–5):** read the claim, look it up in SAP, get the photos, draft the email and send it. It then ends the Run with a terminal hand-off instead of waiting. That can be `request_handover`, or `postpone_case` on a 3-day reminder clock if this is queue-driven.
- **Agent B (Steps 7–14):** triggered by the supplier's reply or by the reminder schedule. It checks once per Run: if there's no reply at day 3, send a reminder; at day 7, escalate to the category manager; if there is a reply, run Steps 9–14 (credit note, tracker, Slack, ServiceNow, archive).

**Next step**
I can invoke `aop-writer` with Build `bld_w01` and this request: "Split the AOP at Step 6 into two Agents. Agent A ends after sending the claim with `request_handover`/`postpone_case`. Agent B handles the reply check, the 3-day reminder, the 7-day escalation, and Steps 9–14." It would work in `aops/<agent-id>.md`.

Meanwhile, check manually whether Mlékárna Polná has replied to the claim sent in this Run. No reminder or escalation will fire for it on its own.
